tweets.text:
12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X

A lot of people I know are moving their posting from LinkedIn to X. When they ask me how I grew 80k followers on X in one year, here’s what I tell them:

1. LinkedIn is a stage. X is a party. First you find your crowd, then you listen to what they're already talking about. Don't start talking until you get it

2. You can't reach the C-suite directly. LinkedIn is a professional network, so you can go straight to decision makers. X doesn't work like that. You have to get mass attention first, and then the right people notice you

3. Post way more than you think. On LinkedIn, 3-5 posts a week counts as a lot. I posted 3 times a day on X for 6 months. Some founders I follow post 5 times a day. It's not that they're on X all day. They just don't overthink it

4. Make posting a reflex. If you spend too long on a post, you won't post. Whenever a thought comes up, post it right there. No planning, no scheduling, no waiting for the right time

5. It's a numbers game. Most posts won't do well. Maybe 1 in 10 will. Maybe 1 in 50 goes viral. That's normal

6. Half your posts should be reactions. LinkedIn is mostly “proactive content”. On X, at least at the start, half of what you post should be “reactive content”: replies, quote tweets, commentary on what others already said

7. Know the difference between a reply and a quote tweet. A reply is like a LinkedIn DM. It says "notice me." A quote tweet uses someone else's content to grow your own account

8. Fix your feed first. If you wanna talk about cybersecurity and your feed is all politics, you can't join the right conversations. Pick a few big names in your niche. See who they follow and who they engage with, and follow those people too. Like, bookmark and comment. After about a week your timeline will look totally different

9. Write like you're texting an acquaintance. Polish turns people off. Everyone's allergic to perfect AI-sounding writing. And please don't use AI or bots to write your replies. People can tell, and they might block you

10. Post the stuff that's obvious to you. Make a list of the top 10 questions customers, investors and your team ask you. That's where you're the expert. What seems too obvious to talk about is exactly what people want to hear

11. Post what you just said out loud. If you say something in real life and people go "huh, never thought of it that way," post it on your way back. Don't wait, you'll forget. You don't have to block out time to think of what to say. Just say what you've already said

12. Show your face, and don't sell yet. X is a wall of text, so video stands out. I just record myself on my laptop with something on the screen. People wanna know you're a real human, not AI slop. And until you have about 1,000 followers, don't promote your company. Share real opinions first. Later, when you repost company news, always add your own take, not PR speak.

Remember: people follow people, not companies

tweets.text:
Huge opportunity right now to build new services firms from the ground up, or transform existing ones, with agents at the center. 

The expertise that services firms in theory should have is as important as ever because you still need deep domain understanding to get the most out of agents. But now the ability to deliver on projects has a 10X multiplier. This means that you can make clients happier, compete to win more of them, go after smaller customers not in the TAM before, or deliver outcomes that weren’t really conceivable.

This is going to happen in advertising, IT transformation, management consulting, finance, and a number of other fields that historically are just fully constrained by the speed of their workforce for output. 

This is a huge opportunity right now for those starting these firms. I wouldn’t count out existing players that commit to the transformation either as existing customer trust goes a long way. But they have to move quickly to make it work.

Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work. 

The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing. 

Next, as this step itself becomes redundant or slows down what agents are capable of, we will be giving agents goals to optimize against and they’ll go off on and increasingly solve larger problems for us. 

This may at first blush look like something whose impact gets stuck with coding, but actually a large percentage of knowledge work may eventually just converge with this form factor due to the massive productivity gains that can be generated. Agents will use computers, leverage our existing tools or write new ones, and write code on the fly to solve larger swaths of knowledge work. 

So even if a task today doesn’t seem to be “coding” directly, the task may eventually fold into being coding adjacent. Manufacturing, architecture, life sciences, material sciences, cyber, and on and on.
 
One big hurdle in the way ultimately will be that much of this work remains non-verifiable, so humans will be even more in the loop than they are in coding. But the part that they can hand off will just get bigger and bigger over time as the models are more capable.

So in short, pay attention to coding and you’ll get a sense for where work is going.

tweets.text:
过去三年，字节、阿里、腾讯是如何绕开美国出口管制，用上英伟达最先进的 AI 芯片的？

中国大厂不直接买卡，海外算力公司负责采购，数据中心运营商负责建机房，华尔街和亚洲银行负责融资。大厂只需签下长期租赁协议，就能远程调用算力。

这门生意有多大？马来西亚柔佛与中国相关的数据中心容量，从 2022 年底的 19 兆瓦飙升至今年 10 月的 1210 兆瓦，增长超过 60 倍。花旗、摩根大通、星展、高瓴等资本巨头均参与其中。

但美国 11 月 16 日出台的新规，改变了整个游戏规则：不再只看芯片卖给谁，而是看最终使用算力的公司总部在哪里。

银行已经开始收紧贷款，部分算力供应商被列入实体清单，数百亿美元的融资与长期算力合约面临重新审视。

动察 Beating 最新深度长文，拆解这条横跨中国、东南亚和华尔街的隐秘 AI 算力供应链，以及字节、阿里、腾讯各自面临的困局。

东南亚的中间人还有机会选边站，但中国互联网三巨头没有。

旗舰基金今年前 10 个月赚了 15.3%，城堡基金（Citadel）准备把约 35 亿美元利润还给投资者。

据彭博社援引知情人士报道，肯·格里芬执掌的城堡基金 @Citadel 预计，投资者有望拿回今年约一半的净收益。

旗下旗舰多策略基金 Wellington 在 10 月上涨 1.7%，截至 11 月初，城堡基金管理的资产约为 780 亿美元。

主动把钱还给客户，是城堡基金控制管理规模的长期做法。2017 年至 2025 年，公司已累计向投资者返还约 330 亿美元。

今年最终返还多少，仍取决于全年业绩。

2018 年，美股下跌时，沃什主张美联储暂停收紧。八年后，坐在美联储主席的位置上，他还会给出同样的答案吗？

据「美联储传声筒」尼克·蒂米劳斯报道，近期科技股抛售加剧了美联储内部的分歧。

继续加息，符合沃什的抗通胀承诺；但按他过去的逻辑，资产价格下跌本身就在收紧金融条件，市场已经替美联储做了一部分工作。

市场目前仍普遍预期，美联储将在 12 月 8 日至 9 日的议息会议上再次加息。

留给沃什的问题是：这轮抛售带来的紧缩，够不够让他停一次？

tweets.text: a november 25 filing says hype, hyperliquid's token, will join the cf institutional digital asset index on december 1. franklin's ezpz fund tracks that index and plans to add hype on or about that date, next to its seven current assets. this puts hype inside a mixed crypto fund, not only in single-token products like grayscale's hypg. the size is small for now. ezpz had $15.46m in net assets on november 11, so each 1% of hype weight is about $155k. the filing gives no weight. the fund can also rebalance by swapping assets it already holds, so the amount of new market buying of hype is not clear.

a glassnode estimate from november 24 found that nearly 90% of leveraged btc long exposure, between spot and the market's average onchain cost basis, had cleared. so fewer longs are left to be force-sold. the remaining forced-close exposure leans to shorts, and closing a short means buying btc. but us spot btc etfs had net withdrawals on all seven trading days from november 17 to 25, $3.05b in total. coinbase takers were also heavy net sellers over 30 days. the estimate came before the rebound, so fresh spot demand behind the move is not confirmed.

thorchain, a crosschain swap network built around its rune token, took $5.65m in gross fees over october 29-november 25. in the 28 days before, it took $1.44m. part of this comes from launderers of the binance theft, and hack-linked swap fees are estimated at up to $1m. little of it reaches rune holders directly: only about $49,400 went to rune burns. a larger share, 20% of system income, goes into liquidity that thorchain itself owns. elliptic data shows about 347,000 stolen eth still unconverted. but when a fault halted most thorchain swaps on october 31, the attackers moved to other bridges.

细思极恐🤯小编在泰国的时候也曾使用过悟空外卖，大家也快检查一下

🚨你在东南亚点份炒饭，App可能在后台扫你相册

苹果在iOS上把一款叫「悟空外卖」（Wukong，也叫Gokoo）的应用直接标记为恶意软件。打开时会弹窗：“包含恶意软件，不能打开。你应将其从设备删除。”

这也不是新鲜事

早在2025年2月就有用户曝光过，把它列入SparkCat恶意软件家族。这套木马专门干一件事：用OCR（光学字符识别）扫手机相册和截图，找加密钱包的助记词和私钥。

你给它相册权限，它就在后台把照片一张张过一遍。看到类似助记词的文字，就传走。

悟空外卖主要服务东南亚华人，泰国为主，马来西亚、越南等地也有。注册用户超13万，月活约5.5万

SparkCat不是只盯这一款app。俄罗斯网络安全公司（Kaspersky Lab）在App Store和Google Play里扫出几十款被植入的应用，外卖、聊天、VPN都有。手法类似：借客服或正常功能要相册权限，拿到后就开始OCR。

目前没有公开的大规模资产被盗数据，但还是千万谨慎小心

tweets.text:
For long horizon LLM tasks, sometimes you’ll come back after multiple hours of work and have no idea what happened.

That’s expected; it’s akin to being on holiday for a week and coming back to your job.

A dastardly simple fix if you’re lost is to tell the model to zoom out:

Zoom out. Assume I have no prior context and I’m seeing all of this for the first time. Explain what’s going on in simple terms. Narrow it down to the most important findings, decisions, or components, and give me a recommendation with a justification if appropriate. If the decision chain is complex, make me an HTML walkthrough to aid my understanding and decision-making.

The alternative version is: I’ve been hit over the head with a rock and have amnesia, please help.

Underlying theme here is that models can get a lot of useful stuff done autonomously. 

You don’t need to be in the loop to read every message and tool call, especially if the work was properly planned. 

But your judgment is still important, so rather than 1) going full Hail Mary/Jesus take the wheel; or 2) throwing away the work because you can’t immediately follow it, just ask the model to lift the fog. 

It sounds super simple, and it is.

It’s not 2024, you don’t need to be some prompt engineer typing diabolical shit like “You are a 165 IQ genius programmer with a girlfriend who loves him and doesn’t care that his crypto port is down 90%…” 

You can just do things.

之前看多加密行情的机构 @glxyresearch Galaxy，昨天也发布了一份研报，撤回了“比特币熊市已结束”的判断，认为从历史周期和市场深度来看，价格有进一步下探可能。

他们结合宏观流动性、机构 13F 持仓和历史熊市统计规律，列出了几个最值得注意的危险信号：

1. bitcoin:native 连续 7 周下跌并跌破 50 周均线，历史统计指向继续探底

报告回溯 2014 年以来的历次熊市数据发现，这种走法从来不是调整结束的终点，一般是熊市进入主跌段或深度磨底的确认信号。

2.美股突发恐慌指数飙升后，比特币往往还要再跌一波

有一个 2011 年以来的历史规律：
每当美股风平浪静三个月以上，突然出现剧烈暴跌、让 VIX 恐慌指数冲破 35时，比特币真正的熊市最低点全部出现在这个情形之后。

眼下美股刚经历剧烈震荡，能否守住 6 月的 59,517 美元周线低点，直接决定了比特币会不会重演历史上的二次探底。

3. 机构短线资金撤退，美股科技股与宏观流动性仍在施压

通过拆解美国机构季末提交的 13F 持仓报告（按真实持币数量计算，剔除币价波动干扰）以及永续合约资金费率、CME 期货持仓，报告发现：
早期涌入的对冲基金和短线套利盘正在持续降杠杆撤离。同时，比特币与纳斯达克 100 及费城半导体指数维持高相关性，在美股科技股回调、美国净流动性尚未重新扩张之前，比特币很难走出独立反弹行情。

4.链上估值与地板模型尚未到达历次熊市极端出清区

虽然全网处于亏损状态的筹码占比正在上升，但综合全网平均持仓成本（MVRV）以及累计价值天数销毁（CVDD）地板模型来看，当前市场还没有跌到 2018 年和 2022 年大熊市彻底出清时的极端低估区间，下方依然留有空间。

至于接下来会怎么走，Galaxy 认为有2种可能。

a. 如果“时间周期”占上风，这轮已经走了 412 天的熊市（已超过 2021–22 年整轮熊市 366 天的跨度）正处在最后一段，时间窗口大约在 2027 年 4 月关闭。

最近的一簇支撑在 48,400 到 53,200 美元，如果在这里止步，这将是比特币有史以来最浅的一轮熊市，也是第一轮没有在全网平均成本线（53,205 美元）下方持续停留的熊市。

b.如果“下跌深度”占上风，市场将向过去历次大熊市结束时的估值收敛，目标区间在 29,100 到 46,100 美元，并且伴随一段持续低于全网平均成本线的煎熬期。

要想证伪这种深熊预期，周线必须重新站回 200 周均线（68,159 美元）乃至 50 周均线（74,401 美元）上方；反之，一旦周线收在 53,205 美元下方，更深的探底就正式打开了。

推荐阅读《对话贝索斯和 Prometheus 联创：携 145 亿美元重返创业，押注 AI 的下一站是实体制造》
